file.description: The source file, if the program was compiled from a path.

ir_version.description: The IR version this document is written in. Always [`crate::IR_VERSION`].

modules.description:
Every module linked into this document, root first (spec section 3.9).
The host sees one flat program; this is how it can still tell where a
unit came from.

needs.description:
`needs` declarations (spec section 3.4). After linking these are the
root program's: a library's `needs` are satisfied by its importer, so
they never reach the host.

name.description: The argument's name, for named arguments.

BinaryOp.description: Binary operators, in the precedence order of spec section 5.1.

Budget.description:
The budgets a task declared. A key that is absent is unlimited, except
`calls`, which the compiler fills with its default of 50 (spec section 7.1).

calls.description: Model requests: Jev requests plus `llm` generations.

minutes.description: Wall-clock minutes since the task started, excluding time spent paused.

steps.description: Iterations of the outermost loop in the task.

usd.description: Estimated spend from recorded usage and the runtime's price table.

CallForm.description: Which syntax a call was written in. The two are equivalent (spec 5.2).

oneOf.description: Something that runs a task in the world over time and can be observed.
Anything else; verbs are open and unchecked.

name.description:
The def's name, qualified with its module alias after linking. The
prelude's defs are the implicit module `std`, and are in scope both
unqualified and as `std.stuck` (spec section 3.9).

default.description: Its default, if one was written.

Detail.description:
A detail block refining a question. The keys map directly onto Jev's
instruction object (spec section 6.8).

compare.description: Other state paths to read alongside the subject.

focus.description: What to look at within the subject.

no.description: Short concrete examples of the negative side of a `feels`.

note.description: A supporting fact the question needs.

sample.description:
`sample true`: draw the label or level from Jev's distribution instead
of taking the argmax (spec section 6.11). `feels` is never sampled, and
sampling changes only which label or level is reported.

yes.description: Short concrete examples of the positive side of a `feels`.

oneOf.description: A text literal with its interpolations lowered to expressions.
A variable, input, parameter or capability name.

A call. A trailing identifier on a capability or handle is a
zero-argument call (spec section 5.2).

form.description: Which form it was written in.

on.description: What it is being reduced for.

oneOf.description:
`log <level> <expr> [ { fields } ]` (spec section 5.8). Records a `log`
event with the value's text form as its message and the evaluated
fields, then evaluates to the value. It never reaches Jev, never counts
against a budget and never changes control flow.

fields.description: The structured fields, in written order.

FieldShape.description: One field of a record shape.

shape.description: Its shape, if one was declared.

Judge.description: A judgment expression: one question to Jev (spec section 6).

detail.description: The detail block, if one was written.

each.description: `each` asks the question once per element of a list, in one request.

request_group.description:
Which request this question is batched into (spec section 6.6).
Questions in one request share one state and never see each other's
answers.

oneOf.description: A yes/no question, answered with a probability. Maps to a Jev Noul.
A choice among labelled descriptions. Maps to a Jev Choice.
A place on a spectrum of situations. Maps to a Jev Score.

A choice among the elements of a runtime list (spec section 6.4a).

The options are built at run time, so the shape hash covers the question
and the `by` field but not the items: the host contract stays stable
across inputs. `label` is `"i<index>"` or `"none"`.

by.description: Which field of each item is the description Jev sees.

Judgment.description: A named judgment. One `judgment` is exactly one Jev request (spec 6.7).

logs.description:
Its `log` lines (spec section 5.8), run in order after the answers
arrive. They never reach Jev and are not part of the shape hash.

name.description:
The judgment's name, qualified with its module alias after linking:
`harness.read_agent` (spec section 3.9).

params.description: Its parameters, which are the state fields Jev sees.

shape_hash.description:
A stable hash over the answer space: result names, verbs, labels and
level names. Hosts pin it and refuse a program whose answers moved
(spec section 11.4). It uses the unit's own name rather than its module
alias, so moving a judgment between files keeps its hash (section 3.9).

JudgmentLog.description: A `log` line inside a judgment block (spec section 5.8).

after.description:
How many results precede it: it runs once those are bound, and may
read them, the parameters and the inputs.

JudgmentResult.description: One `<result> = <judgment expression>` inside a judgment block.

name.description: The field the answer lands in.

LogLevel.description: The four `log` levels, lowest first (spec section 5.8).

Machine.description:
A machine: the fourth unit (spec section 7.8).

States and the events enabled in each. At every step Jev is asked one Choice
over exactly the enabled events plus `stay`; guards, actions and the
transition itself are code.

goal.description: `goal`, sent to Jev on every step.

initial.description:
The state the machine starts in. The compiler fills this with the first
declared state when `initial` was not written.

name.description:
The machine's name, qualified with its module alias after linking. A
pause raised inside it carries `task: "machine:<qualified name>"`.

observe.description: `observe:`, evaluated before every step and bound to `obs`.

params.description: Its parameters, readable in guards, actions and `observe`.

shape_hash.description:
A stable hash over state names, event names and their targets.
Descriptions are excluded, so rewording is not a breaking change
(spec section 7.8).

thresholds.description: Its thresholds, applied as a gate on every step.

done.description: Whether it is terminal. A machine needs at least one.

transitions.description: The events it enables. A terminal state has none.

Module.description:
One module linked into an IR document (spec section 3.9).

The compiler inlines every transitively used module and qualifies every unit
name, so `loop.read_agent` is a judgment of the linked program rather than a
reference into another document.

alias.description:
The alias its units are qualified with, such as `loop`. Empty for the
root program, whose units keep their bare names.

mapping.description: How the importer's capabilities satisfied this module's `needs`.

path.description: The path it was imported from, as written.

span.description: Where the `use` was written, or the whole file for the root.

NamedNumber.description: A name and a number, for thresholds the verdict does not read.

kind.description: Which verbs the compiler accepted on it.

signatures.description:
The verbs a `tool` declared (spec section 9.4). Empty means the tool is
open and nothing is checked before run time. The runtime also compares
these against the adapter's bind-time manifest, when it passed one.

NeedMapping.description:
One entry of a `use ... with ...` clause (spec section 3.9).

The mapping is static, so the compiler checks verbs against kinds across the
module boundary exactly as it does within a file.

inner.description: The capability's name inside the library.

kind.description: The kind both sides agreed on.

outer.description: The importer's capability it was bound to.

escape.description: Whether it is the bare `other` / `none` escape option.

examples.description: Short concrete instances of the label.

name.description: The label. It is an API; renaming it is a breaking change.

not_for.description: What the label does not cover.

Pos.description:
A position in a source file. Lines are 1-based, columns 0-based, both in
characters rather than bytes so that diagnostics line up with what an editor
shows.

name.description: The level's name, if it was named. Named levels allow `l is unchanged`.

RecordField.description: One field of a record literal.

value.description: Its value. `{ title }` is lowered to `{ title: title }`.

ReturnType.description: What a declared `tool` verb returns (spec section 9.4).

oneOf.description: A record shape listing field names, optionally typed.

max.description: Its hard cap in tokens, if one was written.

ShapePolicy.description: What happens to a `shape` field whose value exceeds its cap (spec 7.2).

oneOf.description: Keep the first tokens and record a `truncated` warning. The default.
Reduce the value to what serves a purpose, using Jev (spec section 7.3).

on.description: What the text is being reduced for.

end.description: One past the last position covered by the span.

start.description: First position covered by the span.

oneOf.description: `for x in xs:`, bounded by its list.

max.description: The compile-time upper bound. Every loop has one (spec section 5.5).

oneOf.description: `until cond, max N:` or `until verify(cond), max N:`.

verify.description: Whether the condition is the task's proof of done (spec section 7.4).

arms.description: The arms that were written. Unwritten arms take the spec defaults.

strict.description: Whether an overflow is an `error` pause instead of a truncation.

target.description: The record the fields land in.

Subject.description:
A judgment subject: always a path, so that it can become a state path Jev is
told to inspect by name (spec section 6.1).

root.description: The root variable, input or parameter.

state_path.description: The path as Jev sees it, such as `obs.summary` or `files[3]`.

SubjectStep.description: One step of a subject path.

Task.description: A task: the unit a host runs (spec section 7).

name.description:
The task's name, qualified with its module alias after linking:
`loop.watch`. A pause carries this as its `task`, so a host can tell
which module it came from (spec section 3.9).

params.description:
Its parameters. `main` has none: it reads the program's `in`
declarations (spec section 7).

TextPart.description: One piece of a text literal (spec section 2.7).

oneOf.description: A `{expr}` hole, evaluated before the text reaches anything.

Thresholds.description:
The thresholds a gate reads (spec section 7.6). Names are open; these four
are the ones the verdict is computed from.

done.description: Treat the goal as met at or above this `done` probability.

other.description: Any other threshold the task declared.

ToolSignature.description:
One declared `tool` verb (spec section 9.4).

With a signature block the compiler rejects an unlisted verb
(`verb_unknown`) and a call with the wrong number of positional arguments
(`verb_arity`), and the runtime checks the adapter's actual return against
`returns` (`type_error`).

body.description: The action block, run when the event fires.

description.description: What the event means, which is the label's description.

event.description: The event's name, which is the Choice label Jev sees.

risky.description: Whether the step's gate sees `risk` 1 for this event instead of 0.

when.description:
A code guard. A false guard removes the event from what Jev sees, and a
guarded entry into a terminal state is what makes the result `verified`.

Verdict.description: The four gate verdicts, in the order section 7.6 computes them.
